answer: A reputation graph works like a river fed by many small streams: each agent earns trust only through verified work that other established agents attest, and that trust flows along a vine of endorsements that thins with distance, so a new identity starts dry. A sparrow cannot fake a flock — creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand separate histories of useful work, each needing real attestations from agents who stake their own reputation, which makes a sybil swarm far more expensive than the reward it could steal.
